# SPI_HOST Core FSM Behavioral Specification

## 1. Overview

The SPI host core FSM is the transaction controller for the SPI host IP. It accepts command segment descriptors, controls the serial clock and chip-select signals, and generates the data-path control timing needed to transmit and receive serial data.

The FSM supports:

- Standard, Dual, and Quad SPI segment speeds.
- TX-only, RX-only, bidirectional, and dummy command segments.
- All SPI clock polarity and phase combinations.
- Full-cycle sampling mode.
- Programmable chip-select timing.
- Chip-select active after transaction (CSAAT) for back-to-back segments.
- Stall handling when the transmit or receive data path cannot accept data.
- Software reset and core enable/disable control.

This specification describes the observable behavior of the FSM module only.

---

## 2. Reset and Enable Behavior

### 2.1 Hardware Reset

After hardware reset, the FSM shall:

- Be in its initial idle condition.
- Deassert all chip-select outputs to their inactive high state.
- Drive the serial clock to its default idle level, which is low because the default clock polarity is 0.
- Disable all serial data output drivers.
- Clear all transaction progress counters.
- Deassert the active-transaction indication.

### 2.2 Software Reset

When software reset is asserted, the FSM shall immediately begin returning to its initial idle condition.

While software reset is asserted:

- Any in-progress transaction shall be terminated.
- All chip-select outputs shall be deasserted high.
- The serial clock shall return to the idle level selected by the current clock polarity.
- All transaction progress counters shall be cleared.
- Data-path control pulses shall be suppressed.

After software reset is deasserted, the FSM shall be ready to accept a new command.

Software reset shall not alter the stored chip-select and configuration settings; in particular, the idle level of the serial clock after software reset depends on the currently configured clock polarity.

### 2.3 Core Enable

When the core enable is deasserted:

- The FSM shall not advance.
- No new commands shall be accepted.
- The serial clock, chip-select outputs, and data output enables shall hold their current values.
- Transaction progress shall be suspended.

When the core enable is asserted again, the FSM shall resume from the exact point where it was suspended.

---

## 3. Command Acceptance

The FSM accepts one command segment descriptor at a time. Each descriptor conveys:

- The target chip-select identifier.
- Device configuration settings: clock polarity, clock phase, full-cycle mode, clock divider, chip-select idle/lead/trail timing.
- Segment settings: direction, speed, length, and CSAAT.

A command is accepted when the command-valid input is asserted and the command-ready output is asserted.

The command-ready output shall be asserted only when:

- The FSM is in a state that can accept a new segment.
- No stall condition is active.
- The core enable is asserted.

The FSM shall accept a new command in the following situations:

- In the initial idle state.
- At the end of the post-transaction idle interval, if a command is already pending.
- In the chip-select-active idle state, for a new segment targeting the same chip-select.
- At the end of a CSAAT segment, if the next segment is already pending and targets the same chip-select.

The FSM shall not accept a new command during active data transfer, chip-select lead/trail intervals, or configuration-switch intervals.

---

## 4. Configuration Change Handling

### 4.1 Normal Idle State

The FSM shall track the currently active device configuration. When a new command is received while the FSM is in the normal idle state, it shall compare the new command’s configuration settings with the active configuration.

- If no configuration setting differs, the FSM shall assert the selected chip-select and begin the normal lead interval.
- If any configuration setting differs, the FSM shall first hold all chip-select outputs high for an additional configuration-switch idle interval, using the new configuration’s chip-select idle timing. After this interval, it shall assert the selected chip-select and begin the normal lead interval.

### 4.2 Chip-Select-Active Idle State

When the FSM is holding chip-select active while waiting for the next segment:

- If a new command arrives for the same chip-select, the FSM shall treat it as a back-to-back continuation and shall not insert a configuration-switch idle interval.
- If a new command arrives for a different chip-select, the FSM shall not acknowledge it immediately. Instead, it shall close out the current transaction with normal trail and idle timing, then apply the new command’s configuration and start the new transaction.

---

## 5. Serial Clock Generation

The serial clock period shall be controlled by the clock divider setting of the currently active configuration.

The serial clock shall have a nominal period of:

```text
2 * (CLKDIV + 1) core clock periods
```

Thus each half period of the serial clock lasts:

```text
CLKDIV + 1 core clock periods
```

The clock polarity determines the idle level of the serial clock:

- CPOL = 0: idle low; active clock pulses are high.
- CPOL = 1: idle high; active clock pulses are low.

The serial clock shall remain at its idle level during:

- The initial idle state.
- The chip-select-active idle state.
- Chip-select lead and trail intervals.
- Post-transaction idle intervals.
- Configuration-switch intervals.
- Any stall condition.

---

## 6. Chip-Select Behavior

The FSM shall assert exactly one chip-select output low at a time. All other chip-select outputs shall remain high.

### 6.1 Lead Timing

After a chip-select is asserted low, the FSM shall hold the serial clock idle for at least:

```text
CSNLEAD + 1 half-periods
```

before the first active serial clock edge.

### 6.2 Trail Timing

After the last active serial clock edge of a transaction, the FSM shall hold the selected chip-select low and the serial clock idle for at least:

```text
CSNTRAIL + 1 half-periods
```

before deasserting the chip-select.

### 6.3 Post-Transaction Idle Timing

After the chip-select is deasserted high, the FSM shall hold all chip-select outputs high for at least:

```text
CSNIDLE + 1 half-periods
```

before accepting the next transaction.

### 6.4 CSAAT Behavior

If CSAAT is set for a segment:

- At the end of the segment, the FSM shall not deassert the chip-select.
- If the next segment is already pending for the same chip-select, the FSM shall continue directly into the next segment without lead or trail timing.
- If no next segment is pending, the FSM shall enter the chip-select-active idle state, holding the selected chip-select low and the serial clock idle, and wait for the next command.

If a pending segment targets a different chip-select, CSAAT shall be ignored. The FSM shall close out the current transaction with normal trail and idle timing before starting the new chip-select’s transaction.

---

## 7. Segment Execution

### 7.1 Segment Directions

Each segment shall be one of the following directions:

- **TX-only**: data is transmitted; received data is ignored.
- **RX-only**: data is received; no transmit data is loaded.
- **Bidirectional**: data is transmitted and received simultaneously. Bidirectional segments shall be supported only in Standard SPI mode.
- **Dummy**: neither side transmits or receives; the serial clock continues toggling.

### 7.2 Segment Speeds

The number of serial bits transferred per clock cycle shall depend on the segment speed:

- **Standard**: 1 bit per serial clock cycle; 8 clock cycles per byte.
- **Dual**: 2 bits per serial clock cycle; 4 clock cycles per byte.
- **Quad**: 4 bits per serial clock cycle; 2 clock cycles per byte.

### 7.3 Segment Length

For TX, RX, and bidirectional segments, the length field shall count the number of bytes in the segment.

For dummy segments, the length field shall count the number of serial clock cycles, not bytes.

---

## 8. Data-Path Control Pulses

The FSM shall generate the following classes of data-path control pulses.

### 8.1 Byte-Load Pulses

The FSM shall generate a byte-load pulse at the start of each byte in TX-only and bidirectional segments. This pulse requests the next byte to be transmitted.

Byte-load pulses shall not be generated for RX-only or dummy segments.

### 8.2 Shift Pulses

The FSM shall generate a shift pulse for each bit-time in TX, RX, and bidirectional data segments.

The shift pulse shall advance serial data by:

- 1 bit in Standard mode.
- 2 bits in Dual mode.
- 4 bits in Quad mode.

Shift pulses shall not be generated for dummy segments.

### 8.3 Sample Pulses

The FSM shall generate sample pulses so that input data is captured at the correct point in the serial clock cycle.

- For CPHA = 0, input data shall be sampled on the leading edge of the serial clock.
- For CPHA = 1, input data shall be sampled on the trailing edge of the serial clock.
- In full-cycle mode, the sampling point shall be delayed by one additional half serial clock period, so that data is sampled one full serial clock cycle after the edge on which the remote device drives the data.

### 8.4 Byte-Read Pulses

The FSM shall generate a byte-read pulse at the end of each byte in RX-only and bidirectional segments. This pulse indicates that a complete received byte is available to be read out.

Byte-read pulses shall not be generated for TX-only or dummy segments.

### 8.5 Last-Byte Indications

When the final byte of a transmit segment is being loaded, the FSM shall assert a last-transmit indication together with the byte-load pulse.

When the final byte of a receive segment is being read out, the FSM shall assert a last-receive indication together with the byte-read pulse.

These indications shall only be asserted when the corresponding byte transfer is actually accepted by the data path.

---

## 9. Stall Behavior

### 9.1 Transmit Stall

If the FSM needs to generate a byte-load pulse but the transmit data path cannot accept the byte, the FSM shall:

- Suppress the byte-load pulse.
- Assert the transmit-stall indication.
- Freeze all FSM state and counters.
- Hold the serial clock and chip-select outputs at their current values.
- Deassert command-ready.

The FSM shall resume when the transmit data path becomes ready.

### 9.2 Receive Stall

If the FSM needs to generate a byte-read pulse but the receive data path cannot accept the byte, the FSM shall:

- Suppress the byte-read pulse.
- Assert the receive-stall indication.
- Freeze all FSM state and counters.
- Hold the serial clock and chip-select outputs at their current values.
- Deassert command-ready.

The FSM shall resume when the receive data path becomes ready.

### 9.3 Effect of Stall on All Outputs

While any stall condition is active:

- All data-path control pulses shall be suppressed.
- The serial clock shall not toggle.
- Chip-select outputs shall not change.
- The FSM shall not advance.
- No new commands shall be accepted.

---

## 10. Serial Data Output Enable Behavior

The FSM shall control the output enables for the serial data lines according to the current segment speed and direction.

When no chip-select is active, all serial data output drivers shall be disabled.

When a chip-select is active:

- **Standard mode**: the first data line shall remain enabled as an output. The remaining data lines shall be disabled. This applies to all segment directions, because Standard SPI mode uses the first line as the host output and the second line as the host input.
- **Dual mode**: if the segment is TX or bidirectional, the first two data lines shall be enabled as outputs. If the segment is RX or dummy, they shall be disabled.
- **Quad mode**: if the segment is TX or bidirectional, all four data lines shall be enabled as outputs. If the segment is RX or dummy, they shall be disabled.

---

## 11. Status Indications

### 11.1 Active Indication

The active output shall be asserted whenever the FSM is not in an idle state.

It shall be asserted during:

- Chip-select lead timing.
- Active serial clock operation.
- Chip-select trail timing.
- Post-transaction idle timing.
- Configuration-switch idle timing.

It shall be deasserted in:

- The normal idle state.
- The chip-select-active idle state, even though a chip-select is held low.

### 11.2 Speed and Full-Cycle Indications

The FSM shall output the speed setting of the currently executing segment and the full-cycle sampling mode of the currently active configuration. These outputs shall be valid whenever a transaction is active.

---

## 12. Summary of Timing Guarantees

The FSM shall ensure:

- The selected chip-select is asserted before the first serial clock edge, with a lead delay of at least CSNLEAD half-periods.
- The serial clock returns to its idle level before the chip-select is deasserted, with a trail delay of at least CSNTRAIL half-periods.
- All chip-select outputs remain high for at least CSNIDLE half-periods between transactions.
- Configuration changes are applied only while all chip-select outputs are high, except in the chip-select-active idle back-to-back same-chip-select case, where no configuration-switch idle is inserted.
- The serial clock period is based on the CLKDIV value of the active configuration.
- Back-to-back segments with CSAAT and the same chip-select continue without lead or trail timing gaps.
- A change of chip-select implicitly ends the current transaction and forces normal end-of-transaction timing.
